name: Single Leg Hop
description: The single-leg hop is a unilateral plyometric exercise in which the athlete hops continuously on one leg for distance or height, requiring single-leg power production, landing mechanics, and ankle-knee-hip coordination. It develops unilateral lower limb power and is frequently used in return-to-sport testing and rehabilitation as a functional assessment of limb symmetry after lower extremity injury.

execution.starting_position: Stand on one leg with the other leg raised. Slight hip hinge, upper body ready to swing.
execution.setup_instructions: Mark a takeoff line. Use a flat, non-slip surface with adequate forward space.
steps: Step 1: Balance on the working leg with the other leg elevated.
Step 2: Drive off the working leg to hop forward, using the arm on the opposite side to assist.
Step 3: Land on the same foot, absorbing through the ankle, knee, and hip.
Step 4: Immediately rebind forward for continuous hopping or pause for measured distance hopping.
Step 5: Perform equal hops on each leg.
execution.breathing_instructions: Breathe continuously with each hop. Do not hold breath.
common_mistakes: Letting the knee collapse inward on landing
Using excessive forward lean that causes landing on a stiff ankle
Skipping the controlled landing to rush to the next hop
safety_considerations: Not appropriate in early return-to-sport phases after lower extremity surgery without clearance.
Ensure single-leg landing stability before progressing to continuous hopping.
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Maximize hop distance or height. Full foot landing on a balanced single-leg stance.
execution.tempo_recommendations: For power: maximal distance per hop, 3–5 hops per set. For conditioning: continuous hops for 20–30 meters.
coaching_cues: Drive off a stiff ankle — push the floor away
Land with the hip sitting back — not knee over toe collapse
Equal effort and landing on both legs
